note: Noopener Filter has two independent mechanisms grounded in real code: (1) a filter plugin id 'filter_noopener' (TYPE_HTML_RESTRICTOR) enabled per text format, which adds rel="noopener" to <a target="_blank"> in WYSIWYG markup; (2) hook_link_alter() gated by the single config flag noopener_filter.settings:filter_links (bool, off by default; the config object only exists once saved), which adds noopener to Drupal-generated new-tab links. Settings form route noopener_filter.settings at /admin/config/noopener-filter/settings, permission 'administer noopener filter'. No config schema, no plugin types, no Drush, no dependencies. Medium cases read back a live text format that has the filter on and the live filter_links value; hard cases enable the filter on a format and turn on the filter_links flag, verified against live config.

evals.prompt: What attribute does the Drupal noopener_filter module add to links, and to which links does it add it?
evals.expected_output: It adds rel="noopener" (prepended to any existing rel value) to anchor tags whose target attribute is _blank (links that open in a new tab). It only adds noopener, not noreferrer.

evals.prompt: I enabled the noopener_filter module on Drupal 11. How do I actually make it rewrite my WYSIWYG/CKEditor links so new-tab links get rel=noopener?
evals.expected_output: It is a text-format filter. Go to Configuration > Content authoring > Text formats and editors, configure the relevant format, tick 'Add noopener to all links' (filter plugin id filter_noopener), and save. The filter then adds rel=noopener to target=_blank links rendered through that format.

evals.prompt: Besides the text-format filter, noopener_filter can also add rel=noopener to Drupal-generated links (menu links, link generator output). What config key turns that behavior on, and where is the settings form?
evals.expected_output: The hook_link_alter() behavior is gated by the boolean config key noopener_filter.settings:filter_links (off by default). The settings form is at route noopener_filter.settings, /admin/config/noopener-filter/settings, guarded by the 'administer noopener filter' permission.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, exactly one text format has the noopener filter enabled. Inspect the live filter configuration and give the machine name of that text format.
evals.expected_output: The format is noopener_med_fmt: its filter.format.noopener_med_fmt config has filters.filter_noopener.status = true.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, is noopener_filter's global link-alter behavior (rewriting Drupal-generated new-tab links) currently enabled or disabled? Inspect the live configuration to answer and name the config key you checked.
evals.expected_output: Enabled: noopener_filter.settings:filter_links is 1, so hook_link_alter() adds noopener to Drupal-generated target=_blank links.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a text format with machine name noopener_hard_fmt. Using the noopener_filter module, enable its 'Add noopener to all links' filter (filter_noopener) on that format and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: filter.format.noopener_hard_fmt has filters.filter_noopener.status = true (tick the filter on Manage text format, or set the filters array and save).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the noopener_filter module to turn ON the global setting that makes Drupal-generated links opening in a new tab receive rel=noopener. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: noopener_filter.settings:filter_links is set to 1 (via the settings form at /admin/config/noopener-filter/settings or drush cset), enabling the hook_link_alter() rewriting.
